content.title: Tags That Don't Need Bookends
content.hook: You only need two bookends if you are holding up books. A divider line has nothing inside it.
content.context:
In modern HTML, tags with no content like
and
are called void elements. They never have closing tags.
goals: Position divider lines between content blocks

activities.title: Why does modern HTML forbid closing tags like </hr> or </br>?
activities.instruction: Think about what closing tags are meant to do:

hints.text: If a tag cannot hold any content, what would a closing tag close?

content.question: Why does modern HTML forbid closing tags like </hr> or </br>?

options.text: Void elements cannot have child content, making a closing tag meaningless.
Dividers and line breaks must be created exclusively with CSS.
Closing tags are being removed from all HTML elements in future versions.

content.explanation: A closing tag signals the end of content. Since void elements can never hold content, a closing tag is meaningless noise.

feedback.correct: Exactly. No inner content means no closing bookend.
feedback.incorrect: Think about the sandwich: if there is no filling, a second slice of bread makes no sense.

content.title: Void Elements Mastered
takeaways:
Void elements like
and
never take closing tags.

Writing </hr> or </br> is invalid HTML — you don't need a closing tag when there is no content.
